title: Why Rama Shot Vali From Hiding: His Own Answer
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)

captions.instagram:
Rama struck Vali from hiding. And Rama himself gave the reason.

Vali, struck from hiding, asked Rama: what merit is there in striking one whose face was turned away? (Valmiki Ramayana 4.17.13). Valmiki also records Rama's answer: the law of Bharata's kingdom, the wrong done to Sugriva's wife Ruma (4.18.18), and why from hiding (4.18.34-36). Both sides, in Valmiki's own words. Full 14-min video on our YouTube.

Vali's question or Rama's answer: which weighs more for you?

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)
Verses:
• "Had you fought me face to face, today you would have met Yama. You struck from hiding, like a snake biting a sleeping man." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.17.39-4.17.40
• And at the end, Vali himself grants that Sugriva should have the kingdom. But that he was killed by adharma, that is not right. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.17.43
• "And this is the reason you were slain: Sugriva still lives, and you live with his wife, Ruma." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.18.18-4.18.20
• "Men catch animals with nets and snares, hidden or in the open, whether they flee or stand still." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.18.34-4.18.35
• "Royal sages hunt too. And you are a shakhamriga, a creature of the forest. So, fighting or not fighting, you fell to my arrow." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.18.36
